0:00–0:30 — Which fusion is worth testing?
A chimeric RNA joins sequence from two genes. The practical question is which candidate deserves the next experiment. A high score alone cannot answer that. Team Fusion connects a claim to the underlying reads, the designed probe, protein evidence and the primary paper, then proposes a source-linked next check.
Source: README.md; results/review/*/decision.json.

0:30–1:00 — Separate the claims
There are three different questions: is a gene pair supported at the RNA level, what exact junction joins it, and is a protein translated and functional? We reconstructed 479 eligible ordered pairs, including 109 reported NanoString-supported pairs. Those 109 are not 109 verified structures. Unknown support is also not a proven biological negative. Our workflow keeps these layers distinct.
Sources: results/dataset_reconstruction; docs/submission/SCIENTIFIC_REVIEW.md.

1:00–1:45 — What the system actually did
Codex selected and executed twelve bounded checks across three deliberately selected cases. It compared coordinates, inspected available structure evidence, consulted fixed primary-paper passages, and rechecked genuine NVIDIA Parabricks output. That A100 run aligned two million paired short reads. The twelve recorded outputs replay exactly. The scientist can inspect a proposed next step and revise or defer it. This is an evidence trail from actual recorded tool use; the review page is an offline replay, not a live model call. The larger sequencing and folding campaigns are unfinished work unless separately verified.
Sources: results/review/replay_validation.json; results/compute/pilot_summary.json; scripts/review/README.md. No matched CPU speedup benchmark.

1:45–2:40 — The case that makes this concrete
For Psap–Lgals3, six published read identifiers support a candidate gene pair. When we compare the published endpoints with the sequence-mapped probe, the nearest second-parent endpoint differs by 924 genomic bases. This schematic marks the two positions on chromosome 14. We independently reproduced the coordinate calculation from supplementary tables and reference transcripts.
The discrepancy does not establish that the probe is wrong or the RNA is false. The original alignment and coordinate convention still need reconciliation. It changes the immediate question: inspect the source alignment before choosing a junction-specific assay. Our two-million-pair short-read subset does not match this probe junction under the fixed rule; bounded non-detection is not proof of absence.
Sources: results/review/psap_source_audit.json; Supplementary Tables 3/8; GENCODE M28. Schematic, not a scaled genome-browser track.

2:40–3:20 — Evidence can disagree without cancelling out
Gsdmd–Tmem106a illustrates another trap. The paper reports protein and functional experiments. Our cached 118-amino-acid reference-sequence hypothesis produces a low-confidence Boltz2 model, with mean pLDDT 48.7. Its red and blue segments denote parent contributions, not confidence. The picture is not an experimentally solved fusion structure. A weak computational model cannot erase published experimental evidence. We preserve both facts and specify the remaining question for a new sample.
Sources: results/structures/METHODS.md; results/review/gsdmd-tmem106a/decision.json; Venezia et al., Nature (2026), Figures 3–4, https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-10982-x.

3:20–4:05 — An honest evaluation
We also tested whether adding Hi-C improves prioritisation. On the same 401 complete-evidence pairs, held-out average precision was 0.296 for RNA features and 0.300 with Hi-C. The bars use a zero-to-one scale. The difference is small and the paired gene-component bootstrap interval spans zero. Five-fold evaluation separates shared parent genes across folds. We therefore do not claim an established ranking gain. These retrospective labels measure reported NanoString support, not absolute RNA authenticity.
Source: results/classifier/metrics.json. Exact delta 0.003643; interval [-0.031044,0.046886]. The bootstrap holds model predictions fixed rather than refitting.

4:05–4:50 — The contribution and next validation
The deliverable is a source-linked evidence-review workflow with three concrete cases, twelve exact tool replays, thirty passing tests and a public reproducible release. It makes the basis for the next decision inspectable. The next validation is to reconcile original alignments, have independent scientists review the recommendations, and measure whether this improves decisions. We have completed an AI scientific review; independent human review and measured utility remain open. Another team can download the release and reproduce the key calculations. We have ten seconds of buffer for the five-minute slot.
Source: STATUS.md; results/reproduction/bundle_validation.json. No measured time-saving or prospective utility claim.
